references.text: This day shall be a memorial for you, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord. This is an eternal statute throughout your generations.
Moses reminds the people to remember this day when they went out of Egypt, from the house of slavery, with a strong hand.
The commandment to keep this statute at the appointed time, year after year, as a sign of deliverance from Egypt.
The instruction to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in the month of Abib, when Israel went out of Egypt.
Repetition of the command regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib, as a memorial of the exodus from Egypt.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread begins on the fifteenth day of that same month, and for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
Moses repeats the command to observe Passover in the month of Abib, with unleavened bread for seven days, as a memorial of the exodus from Egypt.
The description of the hosts of Israel who went out of Egypt under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
Paul refers to Christ as our Passover lamb and urges us to celebrate the feast with unleavened bread in sincerity and truth.
Explains the theological reason for the feast: the memory of the haste and urgency of the exodus from Egypt.
